It runs the liquidity component's scout, checks the top candidates' tokens and numbers against independent sources, and writes a ranked recommendation. Use for "find the best pools", "which pool should my idle coins go into", "re-check the scout", or before raising allocator limits. Read-only: it never signs, deploys or changes the daemon's config.

files.name: cointegration.py
files.title: MacKinnon (1994/2010) critical values for the ADF t-statistic, constant, no
files.summary: Engle-Granger cointegration and an Augmented Dickey-Fuller test. This is the machinery `zscore` should have had. A z-score trade assumes the series is stationary; raw SOL price is not, so applying it there is a known theoretical error that no measured result repairs.

files.title: cpcv

files.name: deflated_sharpe.py
files.title: Euler–Mascheroni constant, to double precision.
files.summary: Deflated Sharpe Ratio: the haircut a Sharpe owes to the size of the search. PBO answers "is this leaderboard informative?" The Deflated Sharpe Ratio answers a different question that PBO leaves open: **given that N configurations were tried, how much of this particular Sharpe is simply the expected maximum of N draws?** Comparing a best-of-N Sharpe against zero is the mistake.

files.name: engine.py
files.title: engine
files.summary: Event-driven backtest engine. Bar ordering inside the loop is the whole correctness story: 1. execute any fill scheduled for this bar at this bar's OPEN 2. accrue borrow fees through this bar's close (perp only) 3. liquidation check against this bar's low/high (perp only) 4. ask the strategy for a target, given data <= i only 5.

files.name: fetch.py
files.title: Coinbase's documented row layout. The whole point of naming it.
files.summary: Explicit historical data fetch from the Coinbase Exchange public API. Never called implicitly by a backtest. Run it once to populate the local CSV cache, then every run and every test reads from disk. Two hazards this module exists to handle: 1. Coinbase returns rows as [time, low, high, open, close, volume] -- NOT in OHLCV order.

files.name: gridsim.py
files.title: Jupiter Trigger V2's hard floor. A rung below it is not a small order, it is a
files.summary: Resting-ladder grid simulator — the strategy the extension actually trades. This is deliberately NOT a `Strategy` in the `core.engine` sense. That protocol maps history to one target exposure filled at a bar boundary, and a grid's entire edge comes from **resting limit orders that fill intrabar at known prices**.

files.name: indicators.py
files.title: Multiple of `span` retained when evaluating an exponential recursion. Chosen
files.summary: Trailing-window indicator functions. Every function here takes an array that the caller has ALREADY truncated to bars <= now (a `BarWindow` accessor does this by construction) and returns the value for the latest bar. None of them can see the future, because none of them are ever handed it. Two conventions worth knowing: * Each returns a scalar for the current bar, not a series.

files.name: leverage.py
files.title: Forced-close slippage on top of the liquidation level. 50 bps is an assumption,
files.summary: Low / medium / high margin tiers: run any long/flat strategy as a perp position. A tier is only a leverage multiple plus the venue's cost model. The wrapped strategy decides WHEN to hold exposure; the engine decides what holding it costs at leverage L: open/close fees, slippage, the hourly borrow fee on notional, maintenance margin, and liquidation with an adverse fill and forfeited collateral.

files.name: metrics.py
files.title: metrics
files.summary: Performance metrics with explicitly stated conventions. Ambiguous annualisation is the most common source of a wrong Sharpe ratio, so every convention here is named in the signature and echoed into the report: sample stdev (ddof=1), a 365-day crypto year, and an explicit risk-free rate.

files.name: pairs.py
files.title: pairs
files.summary: Peer-relative-value reversion: trade a cointegrated spread, not a raw price. One mechanism serving two cards. `pairs_cointegration.md` runs it against BTC or ETH, which this repo can fetch keyless; `jlp_vs_sol_relative_value.md` runs it against JLP, whose price history nobody publishes — the code is identical and only the peer series differs.

files.name: perps.py
files.title: perps
files.summary: Jupiter-Perps-style borrow fees, margin, and liquidation. The one thing to get right about this venue: it charges a **borrow fee**, not a funding rate. Consequences encoded here: * Longs and shorts BOTH pay. There is no long-pays-short transfer. * The rate is a product of two non-negative quantities, so it is floor-bounded at zero. No position is ever paid to stay open.

files.name: plotting.py
files.title: plotting
files.summary: Equity-curve and drawdown charts. matplotlib is imported lazily behind a guard so that a missing install degrades to "no charts" rather than failing an otherwise complete run.

files.name: report.py
files.title: Grounding for the multiple-comparisons warning.
files.summary: Comparison reporting, with the caveats the numbers require. A sorted Sharpe table is the most misleading artifact a backtester can emit. Everything here exists to stop that: buy-and-hold is always shown as the baseline, in-sample and out-of-sample are separate columns, and the count of configurations evaluated is printed so a reader can weigh the selection bias.

files.name: scorecard.py
files.title: Component parameters and auxiliary inputs: plain JSON-shaped mappings.
files.summary: Compound five-minute scorecard: score each metric, aggregate into an UP / DOWN / FLAT call. from backtester.core.scorecard import default_config, evaluate, explain, Bars Every component maps visible history to a score in [-1, 1] (+1 = the metric says the next bar closes higher, -1 = lower, 0 = no opinion, NaN = undefined here). Gates map history to "blocked" (no trade, whatever the score says).

files.name: __init__.py
files.title: name -> zero-argument-capable factory producing a fresh, unprimed instance.
files.summary: Strategy registry. Adding a strategy requires a module implementing the Strategy Protocol (see core/engine.py) plus one entry in REGISTRY -- no engine changes.

files.name: advanced.py
files.title: advanced
files.summary: The nine mechanisms that needed code rather than data. Every strategy here was a `spec-only` card whose stated gap was "implementable now — needs code, not data". Each one is deliberately the *simplest honest* version of its mechanism, because the point of implementing them was to measure them, and a nine-parameter implementation measured on one split tells you less than a three-parameter one.

files.name: breakout.py
files.title: breakout
files.summary: Donchian-channel breakout: long on a new N-bar high, flat on an M-bar low.

files.name: buy_and_hold.py
files.title: buy_and_hold
files.summary: Buy-and-hold: the mandatory baseline every other strategy must beat.

files.name: composite.py
files.title: composite
files.summary: Combine several signals into one strategy. This is what makes pair and multi-signal testing possible without writing a bespoke class per combination. Four combination modes, because the choice materially changes what is being tested: * ``all`` -- min of member exposures. Every member must agree. Cuts trade count hard and raises precision at the cost of recall.

files.name: ma_crossover.py
files.title: ma_crossover
files.summary: Moving-average crossover: long while the fast SMA is above the slow SMA.

files.name: rsi.py
files.title: rsi
files.summary: RSI mean-reversion: buy oversold, exit on reversion to the midline.

files.name: signals.py
files.title: signals
files.summary: Indicator-driven strategies. Each class is a thin wrapper over `core.indicators`: the indicator layer does the arithmetic, the class turns a value into a target exposure. Grouped in one module because they are one-screen each and share the same imports; the registry treats them exactly like separately-filed strategies.

files.name: textbook.py
files.title: textbook
files.summary: Five textbook mechanisms that the cited trading guides name and the registry lacked. Source: `tradingstrategyresults.json` (a catalogue of strategies and indicators from public trading guides).

files.name: tiers.py
files.title: tiers
files.summary: Leverage-tier strategies: an existing strategy held as a perp position. The signal is the base strategy's, unchanged and long/flat. The tier supplies the leverage the HARNESS must run it at (`engine_leverage`, see `core/leverage.py::tier_config`).

files.title: Trailing bars handed to the condition code. EMAs forget geometrically, so 600
files.summary: Trigger trading: wait for a mined trigger, enter next open, exit when the context expires. The conditions come from `core/trigger_conditions.py`, the same causal code the miner (`research/triggers.py`) scores, so what is traded is what was measured: * the trigger is evaluated at the CLOSE of bar t from bars <= t; * the target is returned then, so the engine fills it at the OPEN of bar t+1; * the p

files.name: strategy_cards.py
files.title: `measured`     this repo has run it and the card carries the numbers.
files.summary: Strategy cards: one self-contained file per strategy or signal. A card is a Markdown file with YAML-subset frontmatter under `backtester/strategy_cards/`.

files.name: ticks.py
files.title: ticks
files.summary: Explicit trade-tick fetch from the Coinbase Exchange public API. Sibling of fetch.py, and deliberately separate from it. Candles and ticks are different contracts: a tick frame is not a bar frame and must never be loaded as one, so nothing here writes into the `data/<ASSET>_<interval>.csv` namespace that CsvLoader reads. Ticks land under `data/ticks/`.

files.name: trianglesim.py
files.title: (bid, ask, bid_size, ask_size, quote_time); sizes may be None when the source has none.
files.summary: Triangular-arbitrage event replay over top-of-book quote snapshots. `guides/triangular_arbitrage.md` specifies the mechanism; this module is the event replay it calls for. A triangle is USD plus two coins A and B with three markets: `A-USD`, `B-USD` and the cross `A-B` (quoted in B per A).

files.name: trigger_conditions.py
files.title: One condition per group in a conjunction: two conditions from the same group
files.summary: Causal trading conditions shared by the trigger miner and `trigger_trade`. Every value at index t is computed from bars 0..t only (trailing windows, EMAs). `research/triggers.py` mines conjunctions of these; `core/strategies/trigger.py` trades them. One implementation keeps the mined edge and the traded edge the same measurement. No I/O here.

files.title: Bar interval -> seconds. Coinbase granularities plus a daily default.
files.summary: Core value types for the backtester, including the look-ahead guard.

frontmatter.name: VQZL Z-Score
frontmatter.summary: VQZL Z-Score adapts Volatility Quality Zero Line into a normalized regime gauge. The original VQZL apparently required instrument-specific adjustment; this version expresses its readings relative to their rolling mean and dispersion so the author can apply a more comparable scale across instruments. Readings near zero are interpreted as consolidation or choppiness, while larger departures suggest a trending environment. The intention is to keep trend traders away from ranges. It does not establish a trade direction from statistical extremeness alone, even though its bullish and bearish colors make directional readings visible.

frontmatter.name: Supertrend - Ladder ATR
frontmatter.summary: Supertrend - Ladder ATR modifies volatility-based trailing stops to avoid widening their distance during an active trend. It argues that favorable large candles should not determine how far a protective stop sits: long positions use volatility from negative candles, while shorts use positive candles. A second restriction accepts a new ATR distance only when it is smaller, producing a tightening ladder. The intended benefit is a closer stop and earlier exit in strong trends. That is a design aim illustrated by the author, not measured improvement or a guarantee against drawdown.

frontmatter.name: Tensor Market Analysis Engine (TMAE)
frontmatter.summary: Tensor Market Analysis Engine proposes a composite of multidimensional volatility jumps, Hurst-style regime detection and transfer-entropy-like information flow. It aims to choose context-dependent signals and express them through a heavily decorated dashboard and chart layers. It combines mean-return inference with economic-size, power, sign consistency, subsample stability and mean-reversion checks. The output distinguishes strong, weak or absent evidence, making no-evidence a failure to establish drift rather than proof of randomness. Its role is retrospective regime and portfolio research. Several prose claims overstate what small samples or absent drift establish; a zero mean does not imply random-walk behavior, and non-overlapping returns are not automatically independent.

files.name: test_advanced_strategies.py
files.title: test_advanced_strategies
files.summary: Tests for the nine strategies implemented from spec-only cards. Each test targets the thing that mechanism could get *wrong*, not that it runs: the skipped window in dual momentum, the strength gate in ADX, the displacement trap in Ichimoku, the screening rule in the OU reversion, and the regime selection in both switches.

files.name: test_botcli.py
files.title: test_botcli
files.summary: botcli: the DCA bot and the triangle replay run from the command line, offline.

files.name: test_candle_gap_audit.py
files.title: test_candle_gap_audit
files.summary: Gap detection and repair-merge logic in `research/candle_gap_audit.py`. The audit's whole value is the distinction between "this minute was quiet" and "this minute traded and the exchange dropped it", so the tests here pin the mechanics that decision rests on: which bars are reported missing, and that a repaired series replaces the damaged bars rather than accumulating duplicates of them.

files.name: test_coinfit.py
files.title: test_coinfit
files.summary: Economic invariants independent of the coin-fit ranking formula.

files.name: test_compound_backtest.py
files.title: test_compound_backtest
files.summary: Compound backtest runner: data loading, gap handling, engine wiring, IS/OOS honesty.

files.name: test_cpcv.py
files.title: test_cpcv
files.summary: Known-answer tests for combinatorial purged CV and PBO. The PBO cases are constructed so the correct answer is known by design: a signal set where the in-sample winner always wins out-of-sample must yield PBO ~ 0, and one where in-sample rank carries no information must yield PBO ~ 0.5. Without those two anchors, a PBO implementation can be arbitrarily wrong and still look plausible.

files.name: test_cross_asset_cpcv.py
files.title: Deliberately eight mutually distinct metrics. A fake whose median, quartiles and
files.summary: The cross-asset CPCV script's pure parts. No test here loads a price file, runs the engine, or writes anywhere under `research/results/`. That is not tidiness -- it is what makes these tests runnable at all, and safe to run: * `data/` is gitignored, so a test that opened `data/BTC_1d.csv` would pass on a development machine and fail in CI for a reason unrelated to the code.

files.name: test_dcasim.py
files.title: test_dcasim
files.summary: DCA safety-order bot: arithmetic, fill timing, costs, and the one-bar leak guard.

files.name: test_decide.py
files.title: Long enough for the 251-bar warm-ups (`ou_reversion`, `hurst_switch`,
files.summary: Tests for the per-bar rule readout in `research/decide.py`. The readout's one substantive claim is that its target exposures are the same numbers the engine would have acted on. Three tests defend it: * **Engine parity.** A recording wrapper captures every `on_bar` return the engine asks for, and the replay must reproduce that sequence exactly, for every registered strategy.

files.name: test_decide_audit.py
files.title: test_decide_audit
files.summary: Readout trust boundaries over synthetic arrays; no cache/network dependency.

files.name: test_deflated_sharpe.py
files.title: test_deflated_sharpe
files.summary: Tests for the Deflated Sharpe Ratio. The first test is the one that matters: it pins the implementation to a figure the source paper states in prose, so the formula cannot drift into something plausible but wrong. Bailey & López de Prado report that at N=1,000 independent trials with unit cross-sectional variance and zero mean, the expected maximum Sharpe is **3.26**.

files.name: test_engine.py
files.title: test_engine
files.summary: Acceptance tests for the backtest engine. These are known-answer tests, not smoke tests. Each one has a hand-computed expected value, so a failure localises the bug rather than just signalling that something changed.

files.name: test_engine_audit.py
files.title: test_engine_audit
files.summary: Offline counterexamples for money, timing and history-boundary invariants.

files.name: test_fetch_minutes.py
files.title: test_fetch_minutes
files.summary: Tests for the resumable 1-minute fetch. Each class here guards a bug that was live on disk, not a hypothetical one. The fetch is a multi-hour job against a rate-limited venue, so its failure modes are all of the same shape: something is recorded as done that was not done, and no count reveals it.

files.name: test_fetch_minutes_alt.py
files.title: test_fetch_minutes_alt
files.summary: Non-Coinbase 1m fetcher: venue row orders, sanity abort, backward paging, resume, manifest.

files.name: test_full_suite.py
files.title: test_full_suite
files.summary: research/full_suite.py: the plan, and stopping before the sweeps when a fetch fails.

files.name: test_geometry.py
files.title: test_geometry
files.summary: Tests for the block-count geometry sweep. `geometry.py` answers whether the CPCV leaderboard is a property of the strategies or of the block count. Two pieces carry the whole conclusion and are covered here: * **the comparability intersection.** Larger N means smaller blocks means more strategies fail their warm-up.

files.name: test_gridcli.py
files.title: test_gridcli
files.summary: Tests for the ladder-grid CLI. The CLI is a thin adapter over a tested core, so these tests cover only what lives in the adapter itself: exit-code mapping, argument rejection, JSON validity, and the disclaimer. Each one exists because that logic cannot fail anywhere else.

files.name: test_gridsim.py
files.title: test_gridsim
files.summary: Tests for the resting-ladder grid simulator. The load-bearing test in this file is `test_round_trip_captures_exactly_one_rung`. The extension shipped a bug once where the exit rested at the level it had just bought at, capturing zero and paying two fees; `expectedRoundTripUsd` and its JS test exist to keep that fixed.

files.name: test_index.py
files.title: test_index
files.summary: The repository index: isolation, correctness, and the staleness gate. No test here builds the real index or calls the network. `index/build.py`'s `semantic` subcommand is the only thing in this repo that opens a socket, and it talks to localhost ollama; a test that exercised it would be neither deterministic nor available in CI. The load-bearing test is the first one.

files.name: test_index_search_tooling.py
files.title: test_index_search_tooling
files.summary: The index helper scripts: ollama auto-start, the idle rebuild decision, and library search. No test touches a real ollama or embeds anything. Servers, clocks, load and processes are injected or patched, so these are deterministic and offline.

files.name: test_indicators.py
files.title: test_indicators
files.summary: Known-answer tests for indicators, strategies, and the composite combiner. Indicator values here are hand-computed, not captured from a previous run, so a regression points at the arithmetic rather than at "something changed".

files.name: test_interpret.py
files.title: test_interpret
files.summary: Tests for the self-explaining sweep output. `interpret()` turns four numbers into the reading a person should take from them. Its most important job is catching the two dangerous misreadings: * a high positive-count with a high PBO ("lots of strategies work!") * a LOW PBO with a low positive-count ("great, rank generalises!") The second is the subtle one, so it gets the most coverage here.

files.name: test_intrabar_liquidation.py
files.title: test_intrabar_liquidation
files.summary: A liquidation hidden inside a coarse bar must not be rescued by its close. The engine checks a held bar's low/high, but a daily range says only THAT a level was visited. These tests pin the finer-bar walk (IntrabarLayer) and the cases where a daily bar and its hourly bars disagree.

files.name: test_pairs.py
files.title: test_pairs
files.summary: Tests for cointegration and peer-relative-value reversion. The statistics are checked against series whose answer is known by construction — white noise is stationary, a random walk is not, a synthetic pair is cointegrated and two independent walks are not.

files.summary: A Chrome MV3 extension for the owner's Base and Solana money: **holdings, profit and loss, pool discovery, backtests and strategy changes, swap quotes, and alerts** when a more profitable pool or strategy appears. It also keeps an **experimental grid trading strategy on Jupiter (Solana)** with

files.name: fake-soltui-host.mjs
files.title: fake-soltui-host
files.summary: Speaks Chrome's native messaging framing on stdio, over the fake registry. SOLTUI_FAKE_MODE: hang (never answers) | crash (exits at once) | garbage (bad frame).

files.name: fake-soltui-registry.js
files.title: fake-soltui-registry
files.summary: A stand-in for soltui's registry with the same envelope shapes as the contract. It exists so the extension's side of the bridge is tested without Python; the real host is exercised in tools/e2e.mjs.

files.name: cdp.mjs
files.title: cdp
files.summary: Minimal Chrome DevTools Protocol client over the DevTools pipe. Why the pipe and not a WebSocket: `Extensions.loadUnpacked` is only exposed on `--remote-debugging-pipe` (with `--enable-unsafe-extension-debugging`), and the branded Chrome channel ignores `--load-extension`. So this needs Chrome for Testing or Chromium, and it needs no port, no HTTP discovery and no package.

files.name: guard.mjs
files.title: guard
files.summary: What the e2e harness may ask the extension to do. The harness drives the real service worker through `chrome.runtime.sendMessage`. It must never arm the extension, change its mode, create a key or cancel an order, so every message goes through this allowlist first.

files.name: soltui-host.mjs
files.title: soltui-host
files.summary: The soltui native messaging host, for the real-browser e2e. Chrome for Testing runs with a throwaway --user-data-dir, and Chrome looks for native messaging host manifests in <user-data-dir>/NativeMessagingHosts first.

files.name: manifest.json
files.title: manifest
files.summary: Generated JSON object, 12 keys (manifest_version, name, version, description, minimum_chrome_version, background...).

files.name: package.json
files.title: package
files.summary: Generated JSON object, 8 keys (name, version, private, type, description, bin...).

files.name: service-worker.js
files.title: service-worker
files.summary: MV3 service worker — the extension surface of the command registry. There is no long-lived process here. The worker is woken by an alarm, runs one tick, and is free to die. Nothing may be held in module scope that the next tick depends on: everything durable lives in IndexedDB or chrome.storage.local, and the tick rebuilds its world from those plus the venue's live state.

files.name: soltui-transport.js
files.title: soltui-transport
files.summary: Service-worker transport to the soltui native messaging host. Chrome starts `com.mitchhudson.soltui` (soltui/native_host.py) on demand and speaks length-prefixed JSON with it. This file owns what is Chrome-specific about that: the port, the request id, the per-call timeout and the clean error when the host is not installed.

files.name: alerts.js
files.title: alerts
files.summary: Alerts: "there is a more profitable pool or strategy than what you have now". Pure. No I/O, no chrome.*, no clock of its own: the scan in commands.js reads the inputs, and this file decides.

files.name: autoreload.js
files.title: autoreload
files.summary: Auto-reload on update, as a pure decision with injected effects. Once a minute the service worker asks the soltui host for `buildHash`, a SHA-256 over the manifest and src/ of the extension directory on disk. When that hash differs from the one the worker stored, the code on disk is newer than the code Chrome loaded, and `chrome.runtime.reload()` picks it up. A reload kills the worker.

files.name: commands.js
files.title: commands
files.summary: The command registry — single source of truth for every action this project can perform. Three surfaces drive this one registry: extension src/bg/service-worker.js (chrome.runtime messages) CLI tools/cli.js (argv) HTTP API tools/api-server.js (POST /v1/<command>) Nothing may be reachable from one surface and not the others.

files.name: engine.js
files.title: engine
files.summary: The tick. Order of operations is the whole design: RECONCILE before PLAN, always. A MV3 service worker can be killed at any moment, including between "write the intent" and "the venue accepted the order". So the venue's live order list — not our local records — is the source of truth at the top of every tick. Local state is a cache and a journal, nothing more.

files.name: grid.js
files.title: grid
files.summary: Pure grid-strategy engine. No I/O, no chrome.* APIs, no network. Everything here is a deterministic function of (config, price, open state) so the whole strategy is unit testable and a service-worker restart can recompute intent from scratch.

files.name: pnl.js
files.title: pnl
files.summary: P&L accounting. Two lot-matching modes, because two consumers want different answers: PAIRED (default) A sell fill that records the lots its intent was paired with (`closesLots`) closes THOSE lots. Grid exits are placed one rung above a specific buy, so when rung B's exit fills before rung A's, the inventory still held is A's, and strict FIFO would instead consume A and leave B behind.

files.name: risk.js
files.title: risk
files.summary: Risk rails. Every rail is enforced here, in code, as a gate the executor must pass before anything is submitted. A rail that lives only in the README is not a rail. `evaluate()` is pure so the dashboard can show exactly which rail would block a grid before you arm it.

files.name: soltui.js
files.title: soltui
files.summary: The soltui bridge, transport-free. soltui (Python) owns its own command registry and answers every call with one JSON envelope: {"ok": true, "command": "x.y", "result": <json>, "error": null} {"ok": false, "command": "x.y", "result": null, "error": {"code", "message"}} This module forwards a call to an injected transport and hands that envelope back UNCHANGED, so the extension, the extension's nod

files.name: attribution.js
files.title: attribution
files.summary: Licence-required attribution, in one place. The Jupiter SDK & API License Agreement (read 2026-08-04) imposes two display obligations that are easy for a private tool to miss, because nobody else sees the UI: §8.4 the product "shall prominently display to end users ... 'Powered by Jupiter'".

files.name: http.js
files.title: http
files.summary: HTTP layer for the Jupiter APIs. A grid ticking every 30s across N rungs will hit rate limits on the free tier, so retry/backoff and a per-tick request budget are part of the client rather than something callers remember to add.

files.name: price.js
files.title: price
files.summary: Price lookup. Two shapes have shipped across Price API versions (`{ <mint>: {...} }` in v3, `{ data: { <mint>: {...} } }` in v2). The parser accepts either and throws a named error on anything else, so a version bump surfaces as one clear failure instead of `undefined` propagating into order sizing.

files.name: trigger.js
files.title: trigger
files.summary: Jupiter Trigger V2 client. Endpoint shapes below are transcribed from the live docs (verified 2026-11-06, with contract regression fixtures): https://developers.jup.ag/docs/trigger https://developers.jup.ag/docs/trigger/create-order https://developers.jup.ag/docs/trigger/authentication https://developers.jup.ag/docs/trigger/deposit https://developers.jup.ag/docs/trigger/manage-orders Flow: authent

files.name: evm.js
files.title: evm
files.summary: The small slice of EVM ABI encoding the market reads need, in BigInt. Kept by hand rather than pulling in viem or ethers: the extension has zero runtime dependencies (CLAUDE.md, house style), and the reads here are a handful of fixed-shape view calls.

files.name: holdings.js
files.title: holdings
files.summary: Live holdings: what the owner's public Base and Solana addresses hold, in USD. Read-only. No key, no signature, no transaction: Base is read with eth_getBalance and ERC-20 balanceOf through one JSON-RPC batch, Solana with getBalance and getTokenAccountsByOwner, prices from DefiLlama (Base) and the keyless Jupiter price API (Solana).

files.name: net.js
files.title: net
files.summary: Read-only network access for the market modules (holdings, pools, quotes). Everything here goes through `request` in src/jupiter/http.js, so the timeout, retry and JSON handling are the same ones the trading path uses. The fetch implementation comes from `deps.fetch`: the service worker, the CLI and the HTTP API inject the platform fetch, and tests inject a stub.

files.name: pools.js
files.title: pools
files.summary: Pool discovery from DefiLlama yields (keyless, https://yields.llama.fi/pools). Every APY here is QUOTED by DefiLlama, not measured by this project. It includes reward emissions and can be a short-window spike.

files.name: quote.js
files.title: quote
files.summary: Swap quotes. Quote only: nothing here builds, signs or sends a transaction. The extension's signer has no semantic transaction verifier, so live signing stays blocked (CLAUDE.md, "Known-unverified areas"). A quote is handed to the venue's own page, where the owner reviews and signs in their wallet. See Stele KNOW-837.

files.name: tokens.js
files.title: tokens
files.summary: Chains, endpoints and the known-token lists the market reads use. Base: chain id 8453 (0x2105), public RPC https://mainnet.base.org (docs.base.org network table), with base-rpc.publicnode.com first because soltui/wallet.py found it less throttled. Since Denim (Base mainnet, 2026-11-05) the `pending` tag no longer returns preconfirmation state, so every read here uses `latest`.

files.name: fileStore.js
files.title: fileStore
files.summary: Node-side persistence, API-compatible with the browser surfaces. The CLI and HTTP API need the same durability the extension gets from IndexedDB + chrome.storage.local, so this provides: FileStore the Store API (intents, fills, carry, events) on a JSON file createFileArea a chrome.storage.local-shaped {get,set} on a JSON file, so ConfigStore works unchanged outside the browser Writes go through a

files.name: memoryStore.js
files.title: memoryStore
files.summary: In-memory Store, API-compatible with the IndexedDB one. Exists so the tick can run headless — under `node --test` and in tools/dryrun.js — without Chrome or a fake IndexedDB. The engine takes its store as a dependency precisely so this substitution is possible.

files.name: store.js
files.title: store
files.summary: Persistence. Two surfaces, chosen by what the data is: chrome.storage.local — config and limits. Small, synchronously readable at worker start, and NEVER `.sync` (that would push settings, and anything near them, to Google's servers). IndexedDB — the intent journal and fill log.

files.name: charts.js
files.title: charts
files.summary: Charts drawn with TradingView Lightweight Charts, the one vendored runtime library (extension/vendor/lightweight-charts/, Apache-2.0, pinned 5.2.1). The library is imported lazily, on first draw, so node tests and the service worker never load it, and a missing or broken copy degrades to the caller's SVG fallback instead of a blank panel.

files.name: dashboard.js
files.title: dashboard
files.summary: Dashboard shell: hash routing between views, the top bar, the stored scan, and Settings. Views load on first visit and on their own Refresh buttons; Overview paints from the stored scan first so the page is useful before any network answers. Every action goes through a registry command (src/core/commands.js) — this page holds no trading or alert logic of its own.

files.name: popup.js
files.title: popup
files.summary: Popup: holdings and alerts at a glance, shortcuts into the dashboard, and the grid's arm / disarm / kill controls (collapsed: the grid is experimental). All state comes from the service worker over messages. The popup holds no strategy logic — it can be closed mid-tick without consequence, and it must never be the thing that decides whether an order is placed.

files.name: session-key-form.js
files.title: session-key-form
files.summary: Pure helpers for the dashboard's "Create session key" control. Kept free of DOM and chrome.* so the input rules and the message shape are unit-testable. The command in src/core/commands.js stays the authority; this only catches a typo before a passphrase is sealed into a vault that nothing can reopen.

files.name: soltui-panel.js
files.title: soltui-panel
files.summary: Dashboard panel for the soltui command bridge. The command list comes from the registry (`soltuiCommands`), the form is built from each command's declared params by type, and a Run sends only `soltuiCall` with a command name taken from that list. Nothing here knows a soltui command by name, so a new soltui command shows up with no change.

files.name: ui-kit.js
files.title: ui-kit
files.summary: Shared helpers for the dashboard views: DOM building, number formatting, tables, chips and a small SVG line chart. Every string that reaches the page goes through textContent or a DOM attribute, never innerHTML. Token names, pool symbols, venue errors and soltui output are third-party data, and these pages hold extension privileges (KNOW-407): one missed escape would be XSS with real reach.

files.name: view-grid.js
files.title: view-grid
files.summary: Grid view: the Jupiter ladder grid's configuration, risk rails, journal and P&L. Moved off the front page in the 0.3.0 redesign because the strategy loses to buy-and-hold walk-forward (Stele KNOW-605); the behaviour is unchanged. The equity curve is drawn with the vendored Lightweight Charts library (src/ui/charts.js; local file, because MV3 forbids remote code).

files.name: view-markets.js
files.title: view-markets
files.summary: Holdings, Profit & loss and Discover views. Holdings come from the extension's own read-only market reads (holdings); the deeper scan, snapshots, P&L history and the Aero scout come from soltui. Every figure keeps its source label: a quoted APY is never shown as income.

files.name: view-overview.js
files.title: view-overview
files.summary: Overview and Alerts views. The overview paints from the stored scan first (instant, no network), then refreshes holdings live. Alerts come from the background scan (scanAlerts, src/core/alerts.js); this page only shows and acknowledges them.

files.name: view-trade.js
files.title: view-trade
files.summary: Backtest & strategies and Swap views. Strategy work runs in soltui (the backtester is Python): Top 5 evidence, the roster, CPCV sweeps and signal defaults. Swaps are quotes from the extension's registry (swapQuote); signing happens on the venue page (Stele KNOW-837).

files.name: wallet-pubkey.js
files.title: wallet-pubkey
files.summary: "Use soltui Solana address": fill the Wallet pubkey field from the address saved in soltui. The address comes through the same bridge as every other soltui call: the page sends `soltuiCall` for the read-only `wallet.addresses` command, which returns the public Solana and EVM addresses and nothing else (never an extended public key, never key material).

files.name: index.js
files.title: index
files.summary: Venue layer. The grid engine is venue-agnostic: it emits intents, and a venue adapter turns them into orders. That seam exists because the two candidate venues on Jupiter are in very different states of readiness: Trigger V2 — REST, returns signable transactions. Live-capable today. SPOT. Perps — NO public REST write API as of 2026-08-04.

files.name: triggerVenue.js
files.title: triggerVenue
files.summary: Jupiter Trigger V2 venue adapter. Live writes require a trusted semantic-verification signing bridge. The bundled raw session-key signer does not provide one, so it cannot sign remote-crafted money movements. A grid is a ladder of resting price orders, which is exactly what this API is for, and V2 keeps pending orders off-chain so the ladder is not a public roadmap for front-runners.

files.name: signer.js
files.title: signer
files.summary: Signing. Three honest modes, because "unattended bot" and "wallet popup per trade" are mutually exclusive and pretending otherwise ships a broken default: DRY_RUN nothing is ever signed. The signer throws if asked. SEMI_AUTO the worker prepares the transaction and queues it; a human approves each one in the dashboard. Safe, not unattended.

files.name: solana.js
files.title: solana
files.summary: Minimal Solana wire-format helpers. Hand-rolled instead of pulling in @solana/web3.js because the extension needs exactly two things — base58 and inserting a signature into an already-built transaction — and shipping a megabyte of bundled dependencies into a service worker for that is a poor trade. The transaction itself is always built by Jupiter; we never construct instructions.

files.name: e2e-harness.test.js
files.title: e2e-harness.test
files.summary: The browser e2e (tools/e2e.mjs) cannot run under `node --test`: it needs Chrome for Testing. What can be tested without a browser is the part that makes it safe.

files.name: version.test.js
files.title: version.test
files.summary: The manifest version is what the owner sees in chrome://extensions and in the popup header. A change that ships without bumping it looks like no change at all (2026-11-07: the SolTUI panel shipped as 0.1.0 and read as "nothing changed"). CI also fails a pull request that edits src/ or manifest.json without bumping the version; this test keeps the two version fields in step.

files.name: api-server.js
files.title: api-server
files.summary: HTTP API surface. Routes are generated from the registry in src/core/commands.js — the same registry the CLI and the extension use — so no endpoint can drift from the extension's behaviour.

files.name: cli.js
files.title: cli
files.summary: CLI surface. Every command is generated from the registry in src/core/commands.js, so this file contains no per-command logic and cannot fall behind the extension. Add a command there and it appears here, in the help text, and in the HTTP API.

files.name: deps.js
files.title: deps
files.summary: Node dependency wiring for the command registry. The CLI and the HTTP API share this so they behave identically — the only difference between the two surfaces is how arguments arrive. Kept out of src/ because it imports node:fs, which would break the extension bundle if it were ever pulled into a browser context.

files.name: dryrun.js
files.title: dryrun
files.summary: Headless dry run. Runs the real tick — real Jupiter price, real grid engine, real risk rails, real journal — with simulated fills, in Node. This is the integration gate: loading an unpacked extension cannot be automated (chrome://extensions needs a human), so end-to-end verification happens here instead.

files.name: e2e.mjs
files.title: e2e
files.summary: Real-browser end-to-end check. Loads the unpacked extension into Chrome for Testing, drives the real service worker, popup and dashboard over the DevTools pipe, and asserts what a human would otherwise have to click through at chrome://extensions.

files.name: measure-recentre.js
files.title: measure-recentre
files.summary: How often does the shipped auto-recentre gate actually open? node tools/measure-recentre.js --csv ../data/SOL_1d.csv `recentreDecision()` refuses to move the ladder while anything is resting or any lot is open, because `tick()` cannot cancel. That gate is deliberately tight, and the honest question is whether it is so tight the feature never fires.

files.name: soltui-transport.js
files.title: soltui-transport
files.summary: Node transport to the soltui native messaging host. The extension's CLI (tools/cli.js) and HTTP API (tools/api-server.js) reach soltui the same way the browser does: by running the native host and speaking Chrome's framing, a 4-byte little-endian length then UTF-8 JSON, on its stdio.

files.name: verify-endpoints.js
files.title: verify-endpoints
files.summary: Live endpoint check. Confirms the read-side assumptions this extension hardcodes still hold, so a Jupiter API change surfaces here rather than mid-tick. Read-only: nothing is signed, deposited, or ordered. node tools/verify-endpoints.js JUPITER_API_KEY=... node tools/verify-endpoints.js # also checks the keyed tier

files.name: allocator.py
files.title: A backtest on less history than this is "no replay" (metrics.backtest_best reports days == 0 for that), not 0% APR.
files.summary: Put idle wallet coins to work, but only when a pool is worth it. A pool qualifies only when **both** independent estimates clear `min_net_apr`: * the model: income - LVR - rebalance cost at the optimized width (metrics.expected_net_apr); * the replay: the best width on the pool's actual recent price path vs holding the pair (metrics.backtest_net_apr).

files.name: backtest.py
files.title: backtest
files.summary: Hourly backtest of range widths on a historical price path. Model (deliberately simple and conservative): * Earnings while in range = yield_per_usd_day(half_width) * position value / 24 per hour, where the yield curve comes from today's on-chain pool economics (fee or AERO flow per unit liquidity). * Out of range earns nothing.

files.name: chain.py

files.name: README.md
files.title: TradingView Input Optimizer bundle
files.summary: This Chrome Manifest V3 extension automates strategy and indicator input searches on TradingView and stores result tables locally. The directory is named `tradingviewinputoptimizer_v2-7`, but `manifest.json` and the popup identify version **2.3.11**.

files.name: ARCHITECTURE.md
files.title: Architecture
files.summary: The user runs a Chrome extension over a TradingView chart. Content scripts manipulate chart inputs and collect strategy/indicator results. The background worker routes messages across extension contexts. An offscreen page hosts the database worker, and a report tab displays stored results. Registration uses a separate TradingTools service.

files.name: COMPONENTS.md
files.title: Components
files.summary: These are static source roles. Shared globals and obfuscated calls are not a complete typed API. Follow manifest/HTML ordering before changing a dependency.

files.name: DEVELOPMENT.md
files.title: Development
files.summary: Use the supplied local bundle. There is no root `package.json`, dependency install step or first-party compilation command. The `lib/` package manifests describe vendored upstream development and publication tasks, not this component's workflow. Do not install dependencies merely to read or index the bundle. Read the parent rules and component `CLAUDE.md`.

files.name: INSTALLATION.md
files.title: Installation and lifecycle
files.summary: Keep the full local extension bundle and its vendored assets. Use Chrome with extension developer mode and a TradingView page/account appropriate to the intended workflow. Registration/license requirements are implemented by the supplied code and service; this pass neither contacted that service nor tested entitlement.

files.name: MCP.md
files.title: MCP and local tools
files.summary: This component defines no MCP server, tool registry or local MCP configuration. The machine's global AI hub and Stele connectors are external agent services. Their presence does not add an optimizer runtime interface. The parent hub file search may exclude vendor/generated artifacts and the ignored bundle. Use the scoped retrieval store described in `RETRIEVAL.md` for complete-directory coverage.

files.name: RETRIEVAL.md
files.title: Keyword and semantic retrieval
files.summary: The complete-directory corpus includes first-party source, documentation, all vendored text, source maps, styles, types, metadata and SVG text. PNG/WASM/non-UTF-8 files receive metadata/hash records; their binary payload is not semantically searchable. Private `.remember` records, OS metadata and Git internals are excluded. The source snapshot and exclusion reasons are recorded per path.

files.name: SECURITY.md
files.title: Security boundary
files.summary: The extension sees chart content and can change chart inputs. It stores preferences and registration identity in Chrome local storage and optimization results in browser storage/SQLite OPFS. The background license POST contains `license_key`, `email` and `machine_code`. Never put real values in documentation, query examples, Git or exported verification receipts.

files.name: TESTING.md
files.title: Testing and evidence
files.summary: No first-party automated test runner, test script or coverage gate is declared in this bundle. `js/classes/test.js` is a browser experiment with a second Scanner; `test.html` references missing relative demo scripts. Vendor tests and vendor package scripts do not prove optimizer behavior.

files.name: caching-and-optimization.md
files.title: Caches, persistence and optimization
files.summary: Chrome local storage holds popup preferences and identity/license-related fields (`js/content/popup_script.js`, `background.js`). The database worker contains SQLite and OPFS persistence plus explicit create/remove/import/export actions. Neither is an incidental cache that a documentation task may clear. The scanner exposes delays, timeout/retry/refresh controls.
